question: According to Census 2011 of India, what was the percentage of Christian communities of the total population in India?
solution:
The Correct answer is__** 2.3%.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census 2011 of India**, the percentage of **Christian communities** in India was **2.3% **of the total population.
 
• The **Census** is a significant source of data on the demographic characteristics of the population, including **religious affiliations**.
 
• The Census of India is conducted every **10 years** and provides a comprehensive overview of the population structure.
 
• Christian communities in India include various denominations such as **Roman Catholics, Protestants, and Orthodox Christians**.
 
• Christianity is one of the major religions in India, with a significant presence in states like **Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Goa, and the North-Eastern states**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Census 2011**__

 __
 
• The **Census 2011** was the 15th National Census since 1872 and was conducted by the **Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India**.
 
• The Census collects data on various parameters like **population size, growth, density, and distribution**, as well as **social and economic indicators**.
 
 
 
• **Religious Demographics**__
 
 
• The **religious demographics** data helps in understanding the **cultural diversity** of the country and in planning for the needs of different communities.
 
• India is home to multiple religions, with Hinduism being the majority, followed by **Islam, Christianity, Sikhism, Buddhism, and Jainism**.
